Geographic focus:
Global; with specific focus on Europe (western, central, Scandinavia, southeastern), US, Mexico, Canada, Maghreb, Horn of Africa, Siberia, central Asia, China, South America, South Africa, northern Australia

Temporal focus:
T1. Historical report YES — August 2026 temperature records documented
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) YES — El Niño expected to intensify toward year-end, near-term food price inflation, ongoing damage assessment
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) YES — tipping points, Paris Agreement overshoot, structural fossil fuel dependency, Amazon/Arctic destabilisation

Synopsis:
August 2026 tied as the hottest month ever recorded globally at +1.65°C above preindustrial levels, per Copernicus. This occurred before the current El Niño — forecast to be potentially the most intense on record — has fully peaked. Europe experienced its warmest summer on record with well-below-average precipitation across western, central, and southeastern regions. Downstream consequences include wildfires, harvest damage, excess heat deaths, food price inflation, and disrupted infrastructure. Scientists and UN officials stress structural climate crisis driven by fossil fuel combustion, warn of approaching planetary tipping points, and call for accelerated clean energy transition.
